_comment: Each Judicial Council form prints who completes it. DV-100 is the request and the filer completes all of it. DV-109 and DV-110 say the filer completes only items 1-2 and 1-3; the rest is the court's, and those fields are marked courtUse in the field configs so no question is ever generated for them. DV-100, DV-109 and DV-110 are always filed together, so those connectors are unconditional. DV-101 and DV-105 are attachments: the form itself says when to attach it, and the connector asks the same question the form does. DV-101 hangs off item 3's 'Do you need more space to describe the abuse?', and DV-105 off the 'Child custody and visitation' box in the list of orders requested - so a filer who wants neither never sees either interview.

forms.name: DV-100
forms.title: DV-100 Request for Domestic Violence Restraining Order

activates.whenLabel: only if item 7f needs more space
activates._why: DV-101 continues item 7f. Nobody is asked whether they need it: the box is ticked when the description outgrows its own, so the connector waits on the field rather than on an answer. whenLabel is what the canvas prints under the connector, because the condition lives in its style and a chain under End otherwise reads as 'always, in this order'.

DV-100 page 13: "If you are asking for child custody and visitation orders, you must complete form DV-105 ... and form DV-140." The same box brings in both, so they are wired to the same answer. DV-140 itself is attached to DV-110 and is the judge's order; the filer supplies only its items 1, 2 and 3, and every one of those is a question DV-105 or DV-100 already asks.

forms.name: DV-105
forms.title: DV-105 Request for Child Custody and Visitation Orders

activates._why: DV-105 item 8 says it in as many words: "To ask for orders to help prevent abduction, you must complete form DV-108 ... and attach it to this form." So the form asks the question and the packet obeys the answer - the same shape as DV-105 itself hanging off the custody box on DV-100.

_attachedToNote: attachedTo is what each form says it is attached to, on its own first line - not what switches it on. DV-140 is switched on by DV-100's custody box and printed as attached to DV-110, and treating the first as the second put its six pages into DV-100 item 32. DV-109, DV-110 and CLETS-001 are filed alongside and attached to nothing.
